description: Benign MITRE ATT&CK simulations for blue-team detection testing. Every test emits telemetry an EDR/SIEM should detect, but performs no malicious action. Inspired by Atomic Red Team.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_bash
tests.description: Spawn bash and execute `whoami` — basic shell-execution telemetry.

tests.name: id_via_bash
tests.description: Print uid/gid/groups via id(1).

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_powershell
tests.description: Run whoami inside powershell.exe.

tests.name: encoded_command
tests.description: Run a base64-encoded benign command (T1027 + T1059.001).

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_cmd
tests.description: cmd /c whoami — most common LOLBin probe.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate OS, hardware, and version data after access.

tests.name: uname_unix
tests.description: Kernel and arch via uname; tries /etc/os-release when present.

tests.name: systeminfo_windows
tests.description: Equivalent on Windows: systeminfo.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Local Account
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate local user accounts.

tests.name: passwd_read
tests.description: cat /etc/passwd to enumerate local users.

tests.name: net_user_windows
tests.description: net user — list local users on Windows.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries list running processes after access.

tests.name: ps_aux
tests.description: ps aux — list all processes on Linux/Mac.

tests.name: tasklist_windows
tests.description: tasklist — Windows equivalent.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate filesystem after access.

tests.name: find_recent_files
tests.description: Find files modified in last 24h under $HOME.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate other hosts on the network.

tests.name: arp_table
tests.description: Read ARP cache.

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries probe local network configuration.

tests.name: ip_addr
tests.description: Show interfaces and addresses.

tests.name: ipconfig_windows
tests.description: Windows ipconfig /all.

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries inspect open sockets after access.

tests.name: ss_listen
tests.description: List listening TCP/UDP sockets.

tests.name: netstat_windows
tests.description: netstat -ano on Windows.

techniques.name: System Owner / User Discovery
techniques.description: Identifies the current logged-in user.

tests.name: whoami_all
tests.description: whoami; logname; w (combined).

techniques.name: Software Discovery: Security Software
techniques.description: Enumerate installed AV / EDR.

tests.name: list_av_processes_linux
tests.description: Look for common Linux EDR processes (falcon-sensor, osquery, auditd).
tests.command: ps -ef | grep -Ei 'falcon|osquery|auditd|sentinel|crowdstrike|carbonblack|wazuh' | grep -v grep || echo 'no edr processes seen'

tests.name: list_av_services_windows
tests.description: PowerShell — Get-Service for Defender/CrowdStrike/etc.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate / Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries decode obfuscated data at runtime.

tests.name: base64_decode_benign
tests.description: Echo+decode a benign base64 string ('CSP-test').

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries pack/encode payloads to evade static detection.

tests.name: encode_script_base64
tests.description: Base64-encode a benign 'whoami' inline.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
techniques.description: Adversaries write a value under HKCU\...\Run for persistence.

tests.name: write_run_key_test
tests.description: Add and remove a clearly-marked CSP test value under HKCU Run.
expected_signals: registry value created at HKCU Run

techniques.name: Scheduled Task / Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries use schtasks for persistence.

tests.name: schtasks_list
tests.description: List scheduled tasks (read-only — no creation).

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: Rundll32 abuse for proxy execution.

tests.name: rundll32_help
tests.description: Invoke a benign rundll32 -> shell32 ShellAbout dialog (closes itself in the script).
tests.command: Start-Process rundll32.exe -ArgumentList 'shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL' -PassThru | ForEach-Object { Start-Sleep 1; Stop-Process -Id $_.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping (SIMULATION)
techniques.description: Adversaries dump credentials from memory (mimikatz, lsass). This test only emits the keyword & file path indicators an EDR should match — it does NOT extract any credential.

tests.name: mimikatz_keyword_simulation
tests.description: Echo 'mimikatz' and 'sekurlsa::logonpasswords' to trigger keyword/string detection rules.
tests.command: echo 'mimikatz sekurlsa::logonpasswords privilege::debug' && echo 'simulation only — no credential extraction'

tests.name: lsass_handle_simulation
tests.description: PowerShell Get-Process lsass — common precursor to dumping. No memory read performed.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Files
techniques.description: Adversaries grep filesystem for credential keywords.

tests.name: grep_passwords_in_home
tests.description: Recursive grep for 'password' under $HOME (read-only, results truncated).

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries download tooling onto a host.

tests.name: curl_eicar_download
tests.description: Download the official EICAR test file from secure.eicar.org via curl.

tests.name: iwr_eicar_download
tests.description: Windows: Invoke-WebRequest the official EICAR test file.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web (HTTP)
techniques.description: Probe outbound HTTP — used here only to demonstrate beacon-like traffic to a public health endpoint.

tests.name: http_beacon_probe
tests.description: Single GET to https://www.example.com and print status.
expected_signals: egress HTTPS connection from non-browser process

techniques.name: Remote Services: SSH
techniques.description: Adversaries use SSH to move laterally between *nix hosts. This test only spawns ssh(1) against a deliberately invalid host with BatchMode and a short timeout — process telemetry is emitted but no authentication or remote interaction occurs.

tests.name: ssh_attempt_invalid_host
tests.description: Spawn ssh against csp-lateral-test.invalid with BatchMode=yes — fails fast on DNS, but EDR observes ssh process_create and outbound TCP/22 attempt.
tests.command: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=2 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null csp-lateral-test.invalid 'whoami' 2>&1 | head -n 5 || true; echo '[CSP] ssh process telemetry emitted (no auth attempted)'
expected_signals: ssh client argv with BatchMode=yes (typical of automation / lateral tooling)
outbound TCP/22 attempt from non-interactive process

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB / Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries reach Admin$ / IPC$ / C$ over SMB to move laterally. This test only enumerates local shares — no remote authentication is attempted.

tests.name: enumerate_local_smb_shares
tests.description: Get-SmbShare locally + net view \\localhost — typical pre-lateral-movement reconnaissance pattern.

tests.name: smb_admin_share_probe
tests.description: Test-Path to \\localhost\C$ — probes IPC + Admin$ access pattern. Fails benignly if not authorized.
tests.command: try { Test-Path '\\localhost\C$' } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] admin$ probe failed (expected unless local admin)' }

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management (WinRM)
techniques.description: Adversaries use WinRM (PowerShell remoting) to execute on remote hosts. This test only probes WSMan on localhost — no remote command is run.

tests.name: test_wsman_localhost
tests.description: Test-WSMan against localhost — emits WinRM HTTP/HTTPS probe telemetry without launching a remote session.
tests.command: try { Test-WSMan -ComputerName localhost -ErrorAction Stop | Format-List } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] WinRM probe failed (service may be disabled - expected)' }

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries copy tooling between hosts inside the network. These tests spawn the typical transfer process (scp / Copy-Item) but the target is invalid so no transfer succeeds.

tests.name: scp_attempt_invalid_host
tests.description: Spawn scp to push /etc/hostname to an invalid lateral target — emits scp process telemetry without a real transfer.
tests.command: scp -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=2 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null /etc/hosts csp-lateral-test.invalid:/tmp/csp-payload.txt 2>&1 | head -n 5 || true; echo '[CSP] scp telemetry emitted (no transfer occurred)'
expected_signals: scp argv targeting remote host (lateral transfer indicator)

tests.name: copy_item_to_session_simulation
tests.description: PowerShell Copy-Item -ToSession to a non-existent PSSession — emits the lateral-transfer cmdlet pattern without an actual session.
tests.command: try { $s = New-PSSession -ComputerName 'csp-lateral-test.invalid' -ErrorAction Stop; Copy-Item -Path $env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts -Destination 'C:\Temp\' -ToSession $s; Remove-PSSession $s } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] PSSession to invalid host failed (expected) — pattern logged in PowerShell ScriptBlock' }
expected_signals: New-PSSession + Copy-Item -ToSession pattern in Script Block Logging
WinRM connection attempt to invalid host

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass-the-Hash (SIMULATION)
techniques.description: Adversaries authenticate to remote services with a captured NTLM hash instead of a password. This test only echoes the canonical mimikatz pass-the-hash command line as a string-detection probe — no hash is provided, used, or transmitted.

tests.name: pth_keyword_simulation
tests.description: Echo the typical 'sekurlsa::pth' invocation pattern — verifies SIEM/YARA string-match rules without performing PtH.
tests.command: echo 'sekurlsa::pth /user:Administrator /domain:CSP-LAB /ntlm:00000000000000000000000000000000 /run:cmd.exe' && echo '[CSP] simulation only — no hash supplied, no auth attempted'
expected_signals: string match: '/ntlm:' followed by hash-shaped value

tests.name: pth_keyword_simulation_powershell
tests.description: PowerShell variant — echo PtH invocation pattern via Write-Host for ScriptBlock logging detection.
tests.command: Write-Host 'sekurlsa::pth /user:Administrator /domain:CSP-LAB /ntlm:00000000000000000000000000000000 /run:cmd.exe'; Write-Host '[CSP] simulation only — no hash supplied'
expected_signals: Defender AMSI may flag mimikatz keywords

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
techniques.description: Adversaries delete files to hide tracks.

tests.name: create_and_delete_file
tests.description: Create a marker file in /tmp then delete it (simulates evidence removal).
tests.command: f=/tmp/csp_test_evidence_$$.log; date > "$f"; ls -la "$f"; rm -f "$f"; echo deleted
expected_signals: file create -> file delete short window
